sources.entry: Swivel - Tap a key mid-drag and drop files on a wheel to convert, crop, compress, strip metadata or share them, fully offline. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/jonathanlotan/Swivel) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Swivel is a free, open-source, offline macOS menu bar app that converts, crops, compresses, inspects and shares files through a drag-and-tap "wheel" gesture, with a matching command-line tool.
summary.what_it_does: Start dragging files in Finder or on the desktop, tap a modifier key, and drop the files on a slice of a radial wheel to run an action. Three rings are available: Convert (Shift), Tools (Command) and Actions (Control). Conversions cover images, video, audio, documents, PDFs and archives, using only encoders that ship with macOS. Tools include resize, crop, rotate, fit-to-size, compress, background removal (macOS 14+), metadata removal, text recognition, and PDF merge/split. Results are written next to the original with Finder-style names and never overwrite files. The same engine is available as the `swivel` command line tool, and as Shortcuts actions (Convert File, Convert to JPEG, Compress, Convert to PDF).
use_cases: Convert HEIC photos to JPEG on a Mac
Compress or fit images under a file size limit
Crop photos to square or 16:9 by drag
Strip location and camera metadata before sharing
Convert video or audio formats offline
Batch convert files from a shell script
notable: Drag-then-tap gesture opens a radial wheel without Accessibility or Input Monitoring permission
No network code; a build test fails if networking APIs are linked
Writes results atomically with RENAME_EXCL so nothing is overwritten
Ships a swivel CLI using the same conversion engine
Shortcuts actions and a Finder Quick Action
caveats: Apple silicon Macs only, macOS 13 Ventura or later per the README
Cannot write WebP, JPEG XL, MP3, Ogg, WebM or MKV because it bundles no third-party encoders
No watch folders and no automatic update checks
